subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel@finoptima.com>, Samantha Park <samantha@finoptima.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Hi Daniel / Samantha —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our 30-min discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. If I missed anything or you want to adjust priorities, please reply inline.

Top pain points you called out
- Unit economics: inference cost is a blocker for broad rollout of embedding + chat features (expectation: reduce per-request cost ~3x while keeping quality).
- Latency variability: p95/p99 spikes during peak hours; must keep interactive flows under ~200ms p99.
- Operational overhead: managing multiple model endpoints and frequent quantization experiments is slowing your team down.

Current stack
- Inference on AWS SageMaker endpoints (mixed CPU/GPU), some models hosted via a managed LLM provider for burst capacity.
- Batching currently ad-hoc in app layer; no centralized prefix/KV cache.
- Monitoring: basic CloudWatch metrics and internal dashboards; no token-level cost breakdown.

Success criteria for an initial PoC
- 2–4x reduction in per-token inference cost for the primary reranking/embedding pipelines (measured over 30-day baseline).
- 200ms p99 or better for chat reads at 95th percentile of observed traffic patterns.
- No regression in classification/semantic-match quality (>98% of current benchmark).

Technical openness
- You are open to model quantization as long as accuracy is preserved on the evaluated prompts.
- Willing to consider switching to a Redwood-hosted model variant and/or running on dedicated capacity if unit economics and latency SLOs are met.

Requested info / next actions (from FinOptima)
- Baseline usage (tokens/day or requests/day) and typical sequence lengths for chat/embedding flows.
- A short list of 5–10 representative prompts for the quality eval.
- Any security/compliance constraints (SOC2, data residency) to include in an MSA.

Our proposed next steps (Redwood)
1) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Ben (solutions engineering) to scope batching/caching approach and confirm quantization feasibility. (Ben can prototype perf/latency tradeoffs.)
2) Share a mutual action plan + pricing deck (attached) and a short checklist for required data for the PoC.
3) If agreed, run a 4-week PoC on a small traffic slice with concrete success metrics above.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-deck.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx

Availability: I sent a Cal link below — I have availability Wed/Thu next week for the technical deep-dive.

Thanks — looking forward to continuing the conversation.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: Daniel Kim <daniel@finoptima.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samantha Park <samantha@finoptima.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks good and captures everything we discussed. A few quick clarifications from our side:

- Baseline usage: roughly 12M tokens/day across embedding + chat, with peak hour ~2.2M tokens. Average sequence length: embeddings ~512 tokens, chat reads ~350 tokens.
- Quality evals: I'll send 8 representative prompts by EOD tomorrow.
- Security: SOC2 is required; we also have a data residency preference for US-only for the PoC.

We're open to quantization experiments as long as we can validate no material drop in semantic-match. We also want to understand what batching/caching would look like architecturally — specifically how prefix/KV caching would integrate with our current architecture and whether it requires client changes.

I'm available Thu 10:00–11:30am PT for the technical deep-dive. Please send an invite.

Thanks,
Daniel
Director of ML Infrastructure | FinOptima
daniel@finoptima.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Kim <daniel@finoptima.com>, Samantha Park <samantha@finoptima.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Jun 2026 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: inference cost pressure & next steps

Perfect — thanks for the add.

Ben — looping you in to prep for Thu 10am PT. Key asks for the session:
- We'll review Daniel's usage numbers and representative prompts.
- We'll walk through how Redwood's batching and prefix/KV cache plugs into a customer stack (no mandatory client SDK changes for basic integration; advanced cache-hinting can improve hit-rate).
- We'll go over quantization profiles we recommend for 16->8/4-bit workflows and how we validate quality against your prompt set.

Daniel/Samantha — calendar invite: https://cal.com/marissa/redwood-tech-deep-dive (Thu 2026-06-04 10:00 PT). I've attached the pricing deck and a short mutual action plan that lays out timelines and required deliverables for the PoC.

If you want, Ben can kick off a quick perf spike test on a dev snapshot before the session to have real numbers to discuss.

See you on Thursday — I'll send the invite in a moment.

Regards,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
